correctness.rationale: For each occupied n-atom its Sturmian word has k=n rho+O(1), so its full product equals lambda^n mu^k = e^{-chi n} times a factor in [exp(-|log mu|),exp(|log mu|)]. An atom is at most that long. Distinct n-atoms have different last symbols after deleting their maximal common suffix; their initial gap g remains separated under the common suffix by at least g exp(-|log mu|) exp(-chi(n-1)). The source guarantees n+1 occupied atoms; these upper/lower atom scales yield N_K(epsilon)=log(1/epsilon)/chi+O(1). Verified finite mechanical factors, numeric gaps and products from the current standalone package; only proof handles all scales.

value.rationale: The logarithmic cover coefficient is a natural geometric size invariant for Cantor attractors whose dimension is zero; it changes with the irrational rotation frequency under unequal branch slopes. The exact bounded additive error and both-sided metric gap are structural, not an arbitrary numerical increment. It distinguishes dynamically different attractors that the prior dimension-zero result could not distinguish.
